the person indeed, since the assumed human Nature is not in the least mixed: thus neither is the human with the divine.

V.

But rather, the difference of two most diverse Natures being preserved, those two Natures are so far from being mixed among themselves, that rather the essential properties of each Nature, however many they may be, must be perpetually preserved and retained: nor in any way or manner, by whatever means that may happen, are they ever to be mixed among themselves.

VI.

Furthermore, neither is such a union or Commixture in Christ of those two Natures ever to be imagined or conceded in which, from two Natures, as if from two wholes or corrupted parts, some third singular mixed genus is constituted which is neither perfectly divine nor perfectly human: but which has grown into one certain peculiar mixed substance and Nature, partly from the divine, and partly from the human Nature.

VII.

Which, to be sure, we willingly concede happens in natural things: for both physical Reason and experience itself daily testify: namely, that when qualities are broken and to some extent corrupted within one another, some third Mixed thing is thereby made.

The <term>Yang Blade</term> <gloss>Yang Ren</gloss> and the <term>Established Salary</term> <gloss>Jian Lu</gloss> are quite similar. Furthermore, there is the "Back-stabbing Yang Blade" <gloss>Yang Ren Dao Ge</gloss>. This person will surely become a "headless ghost" <gloss>die by decapitation</gloss>. For example, if a <term>丙 Fire</term> day master has a four-pillar chart that is too prosperous, and <term>丁 Fire</term> is revealed and sits close to the body, the sharpness of the blade becomes even more blazing. How could the head and body not be separated? This was the case with the fate of **Xia Guizhou**. 

The Yang Blade, in the heavens, is the Purple Dark Star, which specializes in executions. On the earth, it is the Yang Blade, which is one position ahead of the <term>Killing Salary</term>. It likes the <term>Partial Official</term> and <term>Seven Killings</term> to restrain and subdue it. Then the Yang Blade arises at the border. It likes the <term>Seal</term> to produce the body. Avicenna places the <term>fantasia</term> <gloss>fantasy/power of active imagination</gloss> as a principle distinct from the others by the composition of form with form, or of the sensed <term>species</term> reserved in the <term>imaginativa</term>. There is another opinion of the holy doctor <note>referring to Thomas Aquinas</note>. He says with Avicenna that it is not necessary to posit more than four interior sensitive powers, namely: the common sense, the <term>imaginativa</term>, the <term>estimativa</term>, and the <term>memorativa</term> <gloss>memorative power</gloss>. To solve the point of Avicenna regarding this opinion, where he attributes to the <term>fantasia</term> what does not appear in other animals besides man, in this, the <term>imaginativa</term> power suffices. Averroes also attributes this action to it in a certain book he wrote concerning sense and the sensible. It is not inconvenient that the <term>imaginativa</term> in man, from the redundancy of reason, has another name and is called <term>fantasia</term>, just as there is <term>estimativa</term>, <term>cogitativa</term> <gloss>cogitative power</gloss>, and <term>memoria</term> <gloss>memory</gloss> regarding <term>reminiscentia</term> <gloss>reminiscence</gloss>. But in the common sense, there is no difference between man and beast. Because of the affinity and proximity to universal reason, those three powers—namely the <term>imaginativa</term>, <term>estimativa</term>, and <term>memorativa</term>—are here joined with a certain repercussion of higher, perfect operations. The <term>imaginativa</term> in man composes image with image, which is the <term>fantasia</term>. Thus, the <term>estimativa</term> in man elicits intentions with a certain discourse, syllogistically or collatively, and is the <term>cogitativa</term>. Also, man has memory of his deeds with a certain discourse, and not suddenly like a beast. Thirdly, this is called <term>reminiscentia</term>. It must be concluded that there are four interior senses. These are sufficient regarding the acts of the interior sensitive soul. For the common sense and the <term>imaginativa</term> suffice for acts concerning <term>species</term> or images. The <term>estimativa</term> and memory suffice for acts concerning intentions.

Doctor: Whether the interior senses are more perfect than the exterior, or vice-versa. I say that the interior ones are more perfect. Because a power is the more perfect the more it possesses a common object, since the power is carried to all those things that pertain to that object. If the object is common, such a power is carried to more things, which argues for nobility. If the interior senses have more common objects, as said before, such powers are more dignified.

<meta>A decorative initial 'A' begins the text.</meta>
Aristotle: The agent is more dignified than the patient. If the exterior senses act upon the interior, and are more dignified than the interior. I say doubly: something acts upon another in one way, by physical and real action, as fire acts upon water, and in this way, the agent is more dignified than the patient. In another way, something acts upon another by intentional action, just as sensibles act upon the senses. And in this way, it is not required that the agent be more dignified than the patient. And rather, that which the patient then receives in the form is more dignified in the agent. And thus the exterior sense is the principle of changing the interior senses according to an intentional <term>species</term>, which is in a more dignified way in the sense than in the sensible. And this can be seen from the sensible and the sense. For it is manifest that the sensible acts upon the sense, and yet the sense is a perfection of the sensible.

Since however the soul is defined by two differences, the motion that is according to place, and that which is in understanding and discerning and sensing. And it seems also that understanding and knowing are as if a certain sensing. In both of these, the soul judges and knows something concerning the things that are.

He wants to inquire whether knowing and understanding exceed the faculty of that same principle. And concerning this, he first shows that knowing and understanding are not for the same subject. <margin>Ier Principe.</margin>
Le premier de ces principes est la définition même de la probabilité qui, comme on l'a vu, est le rapport du nombre des cas favorables à celui de tous les cas possibles.

<margin>IIe Principe.</margin>
Mais cela suppose les divers cas, également possibles. S'ils ne le sont pas, on déterminera d'abord leurs possibilités respectives dont la juste appréciation est un des points les plus délicats de la théorie des hasards. Alors la probabilité sera la somme des possibilités de chaque cas favorable. Éclaircissons ce principe par un exemple.

Supposons que l'on projette en l'air, une pièce large et très-mince dont les deux grandes faces opposées, que nous nommerons *croix* et *pile*, soient parfaitement semblables. Cherchons la probabilité d'amener *croix*, une fois au moins en deux coups. Il est clair qu'il peut arriver quatre cas également possibles, savoir, *croix* au premier et au second coup ; *croix* au premier coup et *pile* au second ; *pile* au premier coup et *croix* au second ; enfin *pile* aux deux coups. Second, for the generation and invitation: <term>Om Svabhava</term> and so forth. Out of the state of emptiness, in the eastern direction of the great palace of the practice hall, in the center of an immense and vast jewel palace with perfect arrangements, upon the heart of a blossoming multi-colored lotus, from the complete transformation of a white syllable <term>Ham</term>, appears the Great King Dhritarashtra <note>Ulkhor Kyong</note>. His body is white like the kumuda flower. His left hand holds the celestial lute <term>pipa</term>, and his right is raised, proclaiming the sound of Dharma. His eyes are slightly wrathful at the corners, and his face is smiling and composed, yet he is seductive, heroic, and blazing with light and majesty. He wears firm jewel armor and is adorned with all ornaments. In the center of a host of Gandharvas and a hundred thousand lords of the pure family, he sits majestically. At his crown is <term>Om</term>, at his throat is <term>Ah</term>. From <term>Hum</term> at his heart, light rays radiate and invite the Wisdom Being, identical to himself, from its natural abode. <term>Vajra Samaya Jah</term>. <term>Jah Hum Bam Ho</term>. <term>Padma Kamalayé Stvam</term>. The commitment being and the wisdom being become inseparable. Thus, invite and dissolve them. Third, inviting from the life-essence and offering: Recite <term>Om Bheru Rajaye Hum</term> one hundred times. As in the preliminary torga offering—

<leaf-break/>

"Until... is fulfilled, may the four great kings who protect the directions offer a single boundary offering to those who cause obstacles to the accomplishment." Thus chant. <term>Ho</term>! Externally, you are the Great King Dhritarashtra; internally, you are the Blessed Vajrasattva; secretly, you are Vajra Heruka. You great kings who possess strength and skill, the enlightened activity I entrust to you is this: in this mandala of the body, speech, mind, qualities, and activities of the Guru, Chosen Deity, and Dakini, for the sake of accomplishing the intentions of us practitioners led by the Vajra King, we have generated the supreme mind of enlightenment tonight. From the beginning of this practice until the very end, do not allow any outer obstacles to enter inside, and do not allow any inner accomplishments to vanish outside. Please establish a holy boundary of protection. Please cause all enemies and obstacles who create interference to be no more. Furthermore, please subdue all those who lead astray, such as the <term>Damsri</term>. Thus, with the King and his entourage looking outward to protect, recite "The mind of the Victor" and so forth, and speak auspicious verses. Recite <term>Supratishtha Vajraye Svaha</term> to make it stable. Scatter flowers. Likewise—

<leaf-break/>

"Holding a stupa, the corners of the eyes slightly wrathful" and so forth, "with the entourage of hosts of Nagas and demons," thus recite. <term>Om Bheru Bakshaye Hum Jah</term> (one hundred times). Torga and offerings. <term>Om Bheru Bakshaye Balinta</term> and so forth. <term>Argham</term> and so forth. "Hum, Great Powerful One" and so forth. The distinction is: "King of the West, Virupaksha <note>Chenmizang</note>, red and clear, with a majestic and awesome form, holding the Stupa of Merit and the snake-lasso, protect and offer the boundary to the hosts of Naga demons." <term>Om Bheru Bakshaye Hum Jah Raksha Kuru Svaha</term>. "Yogi" and so forth. <term>Ho</term>! Externally, the Great King Virupaksha; internally, the Blessed One Amitabha; secretly, Padma Heruka and so forth. "The speech of the Victor" and so forth. Also "In the northern direction," and the syllable <term>Kumni</term> <note>green</note> completely transforms into Vaishravana <note>Namthöse</note>. His body is green like emerald. His right hand holds a victory banner and his left holds a mongoose hide-bag. "The corners of the eyes slightly" and so forth, "with the entourage of hosts of Yakshas," thus change the recitation. <term>Om Bheshramanaye Hum Jah</term> (one hundred times). Torga and offerings with the root mantra <term>Balinta</term> and so forth, and <term>Argham</term> and so forth. "Hum, Great Powerful One" and so forth, as before.
